cases.description: 1-byte pointer write + repeated-START read of 2 bytes (baseline indexed_read pairing). Expect W [02], Sr R [02 A0].
cases.xfail_reason: B32 (AD2 path): a write phase that ends in a repeated START is exported as `0x00 W [00]` instead of the real pointer write (162 of 212 in run 2), so the pointer phase is missing and a spurious 0x00 row appears.

cases.description: 1-byte pointer write + STOP, then a plain read (BQ25731 host style, stop-separated pointer). Expect W [04] P, S R [04 A0] P.
Indexed write: register 0x10 + 2 data bytes (34 12). Expect one W phase [10 34 12] P.
Single-byte write with STOP and no read following. With a loopback decoder that has a simple_write rule for register 0x20 on R1, the row must decode as that simple write.

expect.note: Raw bytes must still match exactly; only the decode check is xfail.

cases.xfail_reason: B8: _is_pointer_write() is True for every 1-byte write, so the simple_write branch never runs; the W [20] row's Decode column is empty (the byte is stashed as a pending register) instead of the simple_write rule's text.

cases.description: Write to the address-NAK target (rig.toml [nak], default 0x08 = I2C1's own address with matching disabled). Expect one W phase with an address NAK and no data.
Read of 4 bytes from pointer 0x02 ending in the master's normal final-byte NAK. Expect Sr R [02 A0 03 A0] P; the end-of-read NAK must not be presented as an error.
cases.xfail_reason: B13: the normal master NAK on the final read byte is exported as NAK="NAK" (and coloured as an error) on the read row, indistinguishable from an address/data NAK. B32 (AD2 path): a write phase that ends in a repeated START is exported as `0x00 W [00]` instead of the real pointer write (162 of 212 in run 2), so the pointer phase is missing and a spurious 0x00 row appears.

cases.description: SMBus read-word with PEC: W [08], Sr R [08 A0 PEC], where PEC = CRC-8 over D6 08 D7 08 A0 (Addr+W, command, Addr+R, data). With sniffer PEC validation on, the read row must show a valid PEC.
cases.xfail_reason: B9: the sniffer computes PEC over the read phase only (Addr+R + data) instead of the combined transaction, so the read row shows PEC invalid (✗ PEC) although the bus PEC is correct. B32 (AD2 path): a write phase that ends in a repeated START is exported as `0x00 W [00]` instead of the real pointer write (162 of 212 in run 2), so the pointer phase is missing and a spurious 0x00 row appears.

cases.description: SMBus write-byte with PEC: W [0A 5A PEC], PEC over D6 0A 5A. A single-phase PEC is computed over the right bytes even with B9 present, so this is expected to pass; if it fails, that is a new finding.
Subcommand block read: write subcommand 0x0001 to 0x3E, then read 36 bytes from 0x3E (echo, 32-byte buffer, checksum 0x0E, length 36), the shape DecodeSchema._unwrap_subcommand_block expects.
cases.xfail_reason: B10 (AD2 path only): spy_poll drops continuation segments when fStart == 0, so the 36-byte read is truncated to its first status-call segment; the ion probe captures all 36 bytes. B32 (AD2 path): a write phase that ends in a repeated START is exported as `0x00 W [00]` instead of the real pointer write (162 of 212 in run 2), so the pointer phase is missing and a spurious 0x00 row appears. B10 itself was NOT reproduced in run 2 (36/64/80-byte reads complete); it stays listed until B32 is fixed and the reads can be judged alone.

cases.description: 64-byte read (= ion TXN_MAX_DATA) from pointer 0x00: no truncation on either path.
cases.xfail_reason: B10 (AD2 path only): spy_poll drops continuation segments when fStart == 0, so a 64-byte read split across status calls is truncated to its first segment. If the AD2 captures it whole (xpass), B10's segment boundary lies above this length: record that as a finding and move the case to expect_pass. B10 itself was NOT reproduced in run 2 (36/64/80-byte reads complete); it stays listed until B32 is fixed and the reads can be judged alone.

cases.description: Burst of 200 back-to-back register reads (W [06], Sr R [06 A0]) with no gap: 400 phases. Any drop must be counted by the probe, never silent; the harness requires all 400.

expect.note: A shortfall only at the very end on the ion path would match B11 (IonWorker drain exits immediately); report it as such.

cases.xfail_reason: B30 (ion path): the bit-bang decoder misses one SCL edge under back-to-back traffic at 100 kHz, shifting a phase left by one bit (06 -> 0C, 06 A0 -> 0C 41); 7 and ~10 of 400 phases in runs 1-2, 1 lost. B32 (AD2 path): a write phase that ends in a repeated START is exported as `0x00 W [00]` instead of the real pointer write (162 of 212 in run 2), so the pointer phase is missing and a spurious 0x00 row appears.

cases.description: R1 clock-stretches 200 us before read byte 1 (byte boundary: a hardware I2C slave cannot stretch mid-byte). Data must be intact, and the measured SCL must still match the set speed, because stretched periods are excluded.
cases.xfail_reason: B32 (AD2 path): a write phase that ends in a repeated START is exported as `0x00 W [00]` instead of the real pointer write (162 of 212 in run 2), so the pointer phase is missing and a spurious 0x00 row appears.

cases.description: Traffic interleaved across both responders. R1 and R2 return different word bases (0xA000 / 0xB000), so a mis-routed phase shows up in the value. Note: B30 bit slips are intermittent; LB-15 slipped once in run 1 and passed in run 2, so it stays expect_pass on ion (a slip here is B30, not a new finding).

cases.description: LB-01, LB-03 and LB-06 shapes at 400 kHz. The ion bit-bang decoder is best-effort at 400 kHz (PROTOCOL.md §3.1), so a failure on the ion path is a finding, not a regression.
cases.xfail_reason: B31 (ion path): bit-bang capture fails at 400 kHz (0 of 5 phases in runs 1-2; garbage rows such as 0x00 W / 0x0C R with no STOP) and leaves the decoder mid-transaction.
